tracks.title: Reliability Tasks Derived from SAFETY.md
goals: Increase confidence in sender/receiver correctness, wire protocol behavior, resume semantics, and finalization.
Reduce flakiness and false confidence caused by timing-sensitive test harness behavior.
Separate fast PR checks, extended reliability coverage, and soak-style stability runs.

tasks.title: Stabilize the test harness and remove critical dependence on fixed sleeps
problem: Some integration tests rely on fixed sleeps instead of observable readiness conditions.
This can hide races on fast machines and create flaky failures on slower or busier machines.
deliverables: A shared helper for waiting until the receiver is ready to accept a session.
A shared helper for waiting until an archive, journal, or expected artifact exists.
Removal of fixed sleeps as the primary synchronization mechanism wherever possible.
subtasks: Find all places where sender or receiver startup is synchronized by a fixed delay.
Replace those delays with readiness checks or timeout-bounded polling loops.
Make sure the new helpers work for both push and pull scenarios.
Improve timeout error messages so a failure reports which condition was never reached.
acceptance_criteria: Core connectivity tests no longer depend on a single fixed sleep for correctness.
Timeout failures clearly describe which readiness condition was not met.
Repeated local runs of key tests do not introduce new flaky behavior.

tasks.title: Create and lock down a matrix of critical failure points
problem: There are error-path tests already, but there is no explicit failure matrix tied to expected invariants.
Without a failure matrix, it is easy to miss gaps between transport setup, frame commit, resume, and finish.
deliverables: A list of critical failure points with expected sender and receiver behavior.
A mapping from each failure point to an existing or planned test.
A documented list of known coverage gaps, if any remain.
subtasks: Define failure points before the first FrameChunk, in the middle of a frame, after FrameEnd but before Ack, on checksum mismatch, on trailing bytes, and on invalid message order.
For each failure point, specify the expected state of the part file, journal, final archive, and issue journal.
Connect each failure point to an existing test or create a follow-up coverage task.
acceptance_criteria: Every critical failure point is recorded in a visible matrix.
There are no untracked gaps in the frame loop, resume flow, or finish path.

tasks.title: Expand protocol negative coverage for invalid message ordering and invalid states
problem: Happy-path behavior and some protocol failures are covered, but invalid ordering and invalid state transitions need systematic coverage.
Without explicit negative tests, regressions in protocol validation can slip through unnoticed.
deliverables: Additional protocol-flow tests for invalid packet ordering and invalid state transitions.
Assertions that sender or receiver emits Error and preserves a consistent on-disk state.
subtasks: Add a scenario with FrameEnd outside a valid frame sequence.
Add a scenario with Finish before the frame loop is completed correctly.
Add a scenario with IssueJournalChunk outside its allowed window.
Add any missing negative handshake or role-mismatch coverage.
Verify that protocol documentation matches test expectations.
acceptance_criteria: Invalid message order is rejected deterministically.
Protocol-level failures are covered by explicit tests instead of timing accidents.

tasks.title: Strengthen receiver state integrity coverage for journal, truncate, and rollback
problem: Receiver correctness depends on strict agreement between committed archive length and the persisted journal.
Errors around trailing bytes, checksum mismatch, and partial frames are high-risk because they can silently corrupt state.
deliverables: Tests for discarding an unacknowledged frame.
Tests for truncating back to committed archive_len after verification failure.
Tests for loud failure on irreconcilable trailing bytes.
Tests that journal removal happens only after successful finalization.
subtasks: Cover disconnect after FrameEnd but before Ack.
Cover disconnect in the middle of FrameChunk delivery.
Cover resume with trailing bytes beyond committed archive_len.
Cover incompatible journal versus part-file state.
Verify that uploaded issue journal data never mutates resume state.
acceptance_criteria: Receiver never commits an unverified frame.
After failure, on-disk state is either safely recovered or the process fails loudly.
Journal cleanup only happens after successful finalize-and-rename.

tasks.title: Add archive correctness assertions beyond simple payload hash matching
problem: Payload hash matching is useful, but it does not prove all archive rules.
It is possible to produce an archive with matching payload bytes while still violating path, entry-type, ordering, or finalization rules.
deliverables: Helpers for validating archive-level invariants.
Tests for normalized relative paths, deterministic ordering, and regular-file-only content.
Checks for tar end blocks and correct issue journal behavior.
subtasks: Verify that the tar contains only regular files.
Verify that stored paths are relative and normalized to '/'.
Verify deterministic file ordering.
Verify that skipped files are absent from the archive.
Verify that .issues.tsv is written only when terminal skips exist.
acceptance_criteria: Roundtrip tests enforce archive invariants, not just content hashes.
Archive rule violations produce clear test failures.

tasks.title: Systematically cover live-file retry, best-effort, and skip semantics
problem: Best-effort live-file handling is critical for correctness but easy to break silently.
Growth, truncation, open failure, share violation, and terminal skip cases need explicit coverage.
deliverables: Fault-style tests for unstable live files.
Assertions for clean versus best_effort versus skip classification in sender reporting.
Validation that live-file behavior remains consistent with resume semantics.
subtasks: Simulate a file that grows after open and verify reading stops at size_at_open.
Simulate early EOF and verify the sender retries from the start of the file.
Simulate open failure or share violation and verify correct skip classification.
Verify that a file sent after one or two failed attempts is classified as best_effort.
Verify that terminal skips do not create endless retry loops across reconnects.
acceptance_criteria: Live-file tests match the documented best-effort semantics.
SendReport and receiver state remain consistent for retry and skip scenarios.

tasks.title: Expand binary end-to-end coverage for push, pull, token, dump-id, and warning scenarios
problem: The real CLI matrix needs more explicit binary-level validation across supported transport and reporting modes.
One push test and one pull test are not enough as a long-term safety signal.
deliverables: Expanded binary roundtrip coverage for the supported CLI and transport matrix.
Coverage for warning-mode scenarios that generate issue journal output.
subtasks: Cover push and pull binary roundtrips.
Cover runs with token and without token.
Cover dump-id fallback when dump-id is not provided.
Cover boundary and mixed fixtures.
Cover completed_with_warnings with issue journal persistence.
acceptance_criteria: The supported transport matrix is covered by binary tests.
CLI behavior remains aligned with repository documentation.

tasks.title: Split the reliability strategy into fast PR checks and an extended suite
problem: A single flat test strategy is both too weak for true reliability confidence and too expensive for every PR.
A tiered approach is needed so engineers know what must run for a PR, a large refactor, or a release.
deliverables: A defined Tier 1 fast gate and Tier 2 extended reliability suite.
Documented commands or workflows for each level.
subtasks: Define a fast PR gate with the minimum critical regressions covered.
Define an extended suite for pre-merge, release, and nightly runs.
Document how to run each tier.
acceptance_criteria: The project has a documented tiered reliability strategy.
Engineers can tell which test set to run for each development stage.

tasks.title: Add a soak mode for rare race conditions and flaky failure detection
problem: Single test runs do not reliably expose rare timing bugs, races, or cross-test contamination.
The project needs a repeatable long-run mode for critical reliability scenarios.
deliverables: A separate soak entrypoint or script.
Iteration, seed, and scenario logging for failures.
A documented minimum soak set of critical tests.
subtasks: Select the critical scenarios that belong in the soak set.
Create a convenient local soak command with configurable repeat count.
Create a CI or nightly soak entrypoint.
Preserve useful diagnostics on failure.
acceptance_criteria: The repository provides a repeatable soak mode for local and CI use.
Failures report iteration context and the scenario that failed.

tasks.title: Define final reliability acceptance criteria and documentation sync rules
problem: Even strong tests lose value if reliability expectations are not reflected in the project documentation.
The project needs an explicit definition of done for safety work.
deliverables: A concise reliability acceptance checklist.
A documented rule that protocol, resume, archive, and test-strategy docs must be updated together.
subtasks: Collect the acceptance criteria into a single checklist.
Verify that repository documentation matches actual reliability invariants.
Document the expectation that docs must change together with behavior.
acceptance_criteria: The repository has a single visible safety definition of done.
README, AGENTS, and protocol documentation remain aligned with implementation and test strategy.

tracks.title: Performance v3 Tasks Derived from PERFOMANCE_V3.md
goals: Replace live path based resume with a manifest-backed sender and receiver model while preserving whole-file semantics.
Maximize transfer throughput without turning RAM usage, sender spool growth, receiver manifest growth, or issue-tail persistence into unbounded resource consumers.
Deliver a Unix openat or dirfd fast path, a correct fallback executor, and a benchmark-driven protocol v3 cutover grounded in measured data.

tasks.title: Freeze the benchmark matrix, datasets, network profiles, and success gates
problem: The v3 plan is explicitly performance-driven, but there is no frozen benchmark matrix that captures throughput, latency, RAM, disk, and recovery costs together.
Without fixed datasets and network profiles, the team can optimize for localhost happy paths and miss regressions on tiny-file, deep-tree, RTT-heavy, or reconnect-heavy workloads.
deliverables: A named benchmark matrix covering million-file, deep-tree, mixed, unstable-subtree, mount-backed, and fallback-vs-Unix datasets.
A named network-profile matrix covering low-latency LAN, moderate WAN RTT, high RTT, bandwidth-limited, and lossy or reconnect-prone links.
A written set of success gates tied to the v3 goals: whole-file correctness, bounded RAM, bounded disk, no full live rescan on reconnect, and no throughput regression in target scenarios.
subtasks: Define the canonical datasets that every major v3 change must be measured against.
Define the network profiles that matter for manifest ack cadence and overlap behavior.
List the required metrics for each run, including throughput, RSS, spool bytes, manifest bytes, issue-tail cost, replay latency, and overlap efficiency.
Define how v2 and v3 results will be compared so that the cutover decision is reproducible.
acceptance_criteria: The repository has a single visible benchmark matrix for v3 work.
The benchmark matrix covers both filesystem shape and network behavior.
Success is defined in measurable terms instead of by architecture alone.

tasks.title: Expand the benchmark and observability harness for v3-specific metrics
problem: Existing benchmark entrypoints do not yet expose all v3 costs, especially manifest build and transfer phases, issue-tail persistence, replay latency, or overlap efficiency.
If the harness only reports end-to-end throughput, v3 can accidentally regress time-to-first-frame, manifest fsync overhead, or receiver-side disk behavior without being noticed.
deliverables: Benchmark output that includes sender and receiver CPU, sender and receiver RSS, sender spool bytes written and read, receiver manifest bytes persisted, issue-tail persistence cost, and overlap efficiency.
Support for running the matrix under the required network profiles or an equivalent reproducible shaping mechanism.
Result artifacts that are easy to diff across v2 and v3 runs.
subtasks: Add metric fields for manifest build latency, manifest transfer latency, archive transfer latency, checkpoint replay latency, and manifest ack cadence.
Add sender and receiver disk-budget metrics that expose spool and manifest storage growth explicitly.
Add support for latency, bandwidth, and lossy-link shaping or equivalent deterministic network emulation in the bench harness.
Make sure the benchmark result schema can be consumed repeatedly without manual parsing.
acceptance_criteria: Benchmark output exposes the full v3 metric set from PERFOMANCE_V3.md.
The matrix can be run on more than one network profile without custom ad hoc commands.
Comparing v2 and v3 no longer requires hand-built scripts or manual stopwatch work.

tasks.title: Define the canonical manifest record grammar and local spool format
problem: The current sender model is built around live traversal and file_index assignment, not around a canonical discovery log.
Without a hard local grammar for records, checkpoint replay, path reconstruction, and future protocol design will stay ambiguous and expensive.
deliverables: A canonical set of local record kinds for DirectoryEnter, DirectoryLeave, File, Symlink, DiscoverySkip, and SubtreeSkip.
A binary local spool format that stores record_seq, kind, depth, name, and optional payload without storing full relative paths as the base format.
A documented rule set for deterministic DFS ordering and legal record transitions.
subtasks: Define the binary layout for each local record and the minimum payload needed for replay and diagnostics.
Define how record_seq and work_ordinal relate to each record kind.
Define how symlink targets, discovery skip reasons, and subtree skip reasons are encoded.
Define which record sequences are legal and which are invalid by construction.
acceptance_criteria: The local manifest grammar is explicit enough to implement without guessing.
The grammar preserves deterministic DFS ordering and whole-file semantics.
The local format does not require a full rel_path String per entry in RAM.

tasks.title: Define source identity and manifest.meta state transitions
problem: Spool reuse is dangerous unless the sender can prove that the spool belongs to the same source and the same builder semantics.
The v3 plan depends on clean or dirty and sealed or unsealed state transitions, but those transitions are not yet represented in runtime state.
deliverables: A manifest.meta model that records dump_id, spool format version, source identity, root source path, build state, last_record_seq, last_work_ordinal, last_checkpoint_seq, clean or dirty state, and sealed or unsealed state.
A validation path that rejects reuse when root identity or builder identity does not match.
An explicit state-transition map for meta updates during build, recovery, finalize, and invalidation.
subtasks: Define the minimum source identity payload required for safe reuse decisions.
Define when clean changes to dirty and when unsealed changes to sealed.
Define how invalidation reasons are represented in sender state.
Define how the meta file is updated without advertising progress that is not durably committed.
acceptance_criteria: The sender never reuses a spool from a different source or incompatible builder version.
Meta state transitions are explicit and testable.
The implementation has a single source of truth for sender spool state instead of scattered booleans.

tasks.title: Implement sender spool append framing, checksums, and atomic checkpoint writes
problem: An append-only manifest without strong framing and checkpoint atomics will fail exactly when v3 most needs recovery, after restarts, partial writes, or disk faults.
The v3 plan requires detection of torn tails and corruption in the middle of the spool, not just that the file still opens.
deliverables: A sender spool writer that emits per-record length prefixes plus per-record checksums or CRC.
Checkpoint files with checksums and atomic replacement semantics.
Recovery logic that can trim torn tails and reject corrupted segments deterministically.
subtasks: Implement write-side framing for manifest.log.part.
Implement read-side validation for per-record integrity and checkpoint integrity.
Implement atomic checkpoint update logic instead of in-place mutation.
Add unit coverage for torn tails, mid-file corruption, and mismatched checkpoint content.
acceptance_criteria: The sender can detect and reject corrupted spool state deterministically.
Checkpoint writes are atomic from the point of view of recovery.
A restart never silently trusts an incomplete or corrupted local spool tail.

tasks.title: Implement sender recovery, invalidation, and cleanup policy for sealed and unsealed spools
problem: The most dangerous correctness trap in v3 is silent continuation of an unsealed live-path spool after restart.
The spool lifecycle also needs deterministic cleanup and observability, otherwise disk use and recovery behavior will become operationally opaque.
deliverables: A restart path that invalidates unsealed live-path spools and only allows continuation for explicitly eligible pinned or snapshotted sources.
Discovery issue events for spool invalidated, spool corrupted, and spool rebuilt.
Cleanup logic for successful finish and GC hooks for old sender-side state.
subtasks: Load manifest.meta and the last valid checkpoint on startup.
Invalidate and rebuild when a live path source restarts with an unsealed spool.
Permit continuation only for the allowed source kinds.
Emit invalidation or corruption events into the discovery issue path.
Delete sender spool state on successful FinishAck and define preservation or GC behavior after failure.
acceptance_criteria: An unsealed live-path spool is never silently extended after restart.
Recovery decisions are visible in sender diagnostics and issue reporting.
Successful runs clean up sender-side spool state deterministically.

tasks.title: Implement sender spool quota, disk budget enforcement, and discovery backpressure
problem: A disk-backed manifest solves RAM pressure only if the spool itself does not grow without limit.
Discovery can outrun frame production and manifest upload unless sender-side backpressure is explicit.
deliverables: A sender-side spool quota or upper bound with explicit behavior on exhaustion.
Backpressure between discovery, spool append, and downstream consumers.
Metrics that expose spool bytes written, spool bytes read, and time spent blocked by disk budget.
subtasks: Define how sender behaves when spool quota is reached: block, slow down, or fail loudly by design.
Implement producer-consumer backpressure between the manifest builder and frame builder.
Expose spool quota and budget pressure in telemetry or observability surfaces.
Make sure quota logic does not violate deterministic ordering or whole-file semantics.
acceptance_criteria: Sender spool growth is bounded by an explicit policy.
Discovery cannot outrun downstream stages indefinitely.
Quota-related behavior is measurable instead of inferred from disk usage after the fact.

tasks.title: Implement sparse checkpoints and checkpointed replay state
problem: A disk-backed manifest only helps throughput and reconnect latency if the sender can seek quickly to the relevant point instead of replaying the entire log.
Replay needs enough saved state to rebuild the path stack and execution state without allocation-heavy full-path reconstruction.
deliverables: Sparse checkpoints that store record_seq, work_ordinal, spool offset, path stack snapshot, and enough execution state for fast replay.
A replay path that seeks to the nearest checkpoint and replays only the small tail after it.
Replay latency metrics suitable for the benchmark matrix.
subtasks: Define checkpoint payload structure and stride.
Store and load path stack snapshots as part of checkpoint data.
Implement seek plus tail replay logic for reconnect and restart.
Measure and expose checkpoint replay latency.
acceptance_criteria: Reconnect and restart do not require rereading the full manifest.
Replay latency is bounded by the configured checkpoint stride plus a small tail.
Checkpointed replay can restore both path stack and ordinal progress.

tasks.title: Refactor sender discovery into a streaming manifest builder
problem: Current sender discovery is still tied to the live tree and file_index assignment, which is exactly the dependency v3 is trying to remove.
Without a streaming manifest builder, the sender will either keep rescanning or accidentally build a large in-memory manifest.
deliverables: A discovery pipeline that appends canonical records incrementally to the spool.
Leaf-only work_ordinal assignment for File and Symlink records.
A manifest builder that preserves deterministic DFS plus sorted-entry ordering while keeping memory bounded.
subtasks: Replace file_index-centric discovery with record_seq plus work_ordinal generation.
Emit DirectoryEnter and DirectoryLeave records explicitly.
Emit DiscoverySkip and SubtreeSkip records instead of collapsing them into path-only side effects.
Make sure the builder does not require a full manifest Vec or a full rel_path String per entry in RAM.
acceptance_criteria: Sender discovery produces a canonical on-disk discovery log incrementally.
Deterministic traversal order is preserved exactly.
Memory usage stays bounded independently from total source entry count.

tasks.title: Implement discovery-time file type policy and skip reasons in the manifest builder
problem: The current project contract includes virtual-filesystem skips, unsupported special-entry skips, and symlink-target handling, but v3 has not yet moved those rules into manifest semantics.
If discovery-time file type policy is not explicit in the manifest builder, unsupported entries can leak into execution or trigger expensive repeated checks.
deliverables: Cached Linux mountinfo or equivalent discovery state for virtual-filesystem detection.
Kind-specific DiscoverySkip reasons for procfs or sysfs style filesystems, sockets, devices, FIFOs, and unreadable symlink targets.
A rule that only symlinks with readable targets become sendable work items.
subtasks: Preserve cached virtual filesystem detection rather than probing mounts per entry.
Emit DiscoverySkip records with explicit reasons for unsupported filesystem types and special entry kinds.
Record symlink targets in the manifest only when they were read successfully.
Verify that unsupported discovery entries never receive a work_ordinal.
acceptance_criteria: Virtual filesystems and unsupported special entries never become file work items.
Unreadable symlink targets are represented honestly as discovery skips.
File-type policy remains aligned with the project contract while using the v3 manifest model.

tasks.title: Implement manifest-driven sender replay and resume without full live rescan
problem: The primary correctness and performance goal of v3 is to stop depending on a full live rescan after reconnect.
Resume also needs to preserve progress across terminal file skips even when no tar payload was emitted.
deliverables: A sender replay path that resumes from spool plus checkpoint state instead of rescanning the full live tree.
Committed progress keyed by work_ordinal for sendable leaf items, including terminal skips.
Correct handling of root-source failure versus subtree-level discovery failure.
subtasks: Seek to the correct checkpoint based on committed progress and rebuild the execution state from it.
Replay only the required tail and resume leaf processing in deterministic order.
Carry committed work_ordinal across terminal regular-file and symlink skips even when tar payload is absent.
Preserve fatal behavior when the root source disappears before enough manifest state exists.
acceptance_criteria: Reconnect no longer requires a full live rescan for ordinary v3 sessions.
Sender progress across skips remains monotonic and deterministic.
Root-source failure and subtree discovery failure remain semantically distinct.

tasks.title: Implement reusable path materialization for diagnostics, tar headers, and fallback execution
problem: Depth plus name only helps if the hot path does not reconstruct a brand-new full relative path String for every file work item.
Diagnostics, tar headers, and fallback execution still need path materialization, so the cost must be amortized rather than ignored.
deliverables: A reusable path buffer, segment arena, or equivalent mechanism for manifest-driven execution.
A clear API boundary between leaf-name access, occasional full-path rendering, and diagnostic formatting.
Metrics or proxies that expose path materialization allocation cost in benchmarks.
subtasks: Define a path stack representation that can feed both diagnostics and execution paths.
Implement amortized full-path rendering for the places where it is still needed.
Remove avoidable per-item String allocations from the sender hot path.
Add a measurable signal for path materialization cost in the benchmark harness.
acceptance_criteria: Path materialization is not allocation-heavy in the sender hot path.
The fallback executor can use the same path infrastructure as the fast path.
Path materialization cost is visible in benchmarks instead of hidden in allocator noise.

tasks.title: Implement the Unix openat or dirfd executor as the preferred fast path
problem: The current absolute-path reopen model pays repeated path-resolution costs and loses locality on deep tiny-file workloads.
V3 explicitly targets a Unix fast path through openat or dirfd, but the sender still needs to preserve whole-file semantics and live-file policy.
deliverables: A Unix executor that opens regular files through parent dirfd plus leaf name, reads symlink targets through readlinkat, and derives authoritative metadata from opened handles.
A directory-handle stack by manifest depth with bounded FD usage.
Benchmarks that compare the Unix fast path to the old absolute-path behavior and the fallback executor.
subtasks: Add dirfd stack management tied to the manifest depth and DirectoryEnter or DirectoryLeave replay.
Implement regular-file open through openat and symlink target reads through readlinkat.
Preserve the existing live-file retry policy based on authoritative opened-handle metadata.
Integrate the fast path with frame production and direct-stream readers.
acceptance_criteria: Unix execution no longer depends on absolute paths as the primary hot path.
Whole-file semantics and live-file retry behavior remain unchanged.
The implementation measures and enforces its FD budget instead of assuming it will stay safe.

tasks.title: Implement the cross-platform fallback executor on the same manifest model
problem: V3 must not become Unix-only by accident or by hidden assumptions in the sender execution model.
A fallback executor that requires separate discovery logic would fracture correctness and benchmarking.
deliverables: A fallback executor that consumes the same manifest spool, the same record_seq and work_ordinal model, and the same replay state as the Unix fast path.
Lazy full-path reconstruction built on the shared path materialization layer.
Benchmark hooks that compare fallback cost against the Unix fast path.
subtasks: Define a shared executor interface that both the Unix path and fallback path can implement.
Build lazy path reconstruction for platforms without openat or dirfd style operations.
Make sure the fallback path preserves deterministic ordering and whole-file semantics without a separate discovery code path.
Benchmark fallback execution explicitly instead of treating it as an invisible legacy path.
acceptance_criteria: The fallback path uses the same manifest model and replay state as the Unix path.
There is no second discovery implementation for non-Unix platforms.
Fallback behavior is benchmarked and observable rather than left as a correctness afterthought.

tasks.title: Introduce a source backend boundary for pinned, snapshotted, and ordinary path sources
problem: The v3 recovery rules already distinguish pinned or snapshotted sources from ordinary live paths, but the sender runtime does not yet encode that distinction cleanly.
Without a source backend boundary, spool continuation and invalidation logic will remain ad hoc and spread across unrelated code paths.
deliverables: An internal source backend abstraction that can distinguish ordinary path sources from pinned or snapshotted sources.
Spool metadata and recovery decisions that incorporate source backend kind explicitly.
A clear extension point for future snapshot or pin fast paths without rewriting the manifest model.
subtasks: Add a source backend kind to sender runtime state.
Plumb the backend kind into manifest.meta and recovery decisions.
Keep ordinary path sources as the default behavior while making eligibility for spool continuation explicit.
Avoid making source backend wiring a hidden protocol concern at this stage.
acceptance_criteria: Pinned, snapshotted, and ordinary path sources are distinguishable in runtime state.
Spool continuation eligibility is driven by explicit backend kind rather than by path heuristics alone.
The source backend boundary does not require a second manifest model.

tasks.title: Split sender reporting into file issues and discovery issues with a typed issue model
problem: The current issue model is file-centric and cannot represent subtree skips, spool invalidation, or spool corruption honestly.
If v3 tries to force discovery issues into file skip counters, it will either lie about behavior or reintroduce expensive rescans just to count skipped files.
deliverables: Separate sender-side accumulation for file terminal issues and discovery issues.
A typed issue model with explicit scope, such as file or discovery, and enough data to reconstruct final reporting.
A candidate aggregate set that can replace or augment old counters without hiding discovery semantics.
subtasks: Define the data model for file terminal issues keyed by work_ordinal.
Define the data model for discovery issues keyed by record_seq.
Introduce aggregate counters such as subtrees_skipped, discovery_issues_total, and manifest_resets_total where appropriate.
Update session status semantics so discovery warnings do not pretend to be file skips.
acceptance_criteria: File issues and discovery issues are no longer conflated in sender reporting.
Sender can report spool invalidation and subtree-level problems honestly.
Aggregate reporting no longer depends on fake rescans or guessed subtree sizes.

tasks.title: Implement receiver-side manifest store, boundary journaling, and integrity framing
problem: Protocol v3 needs receiver-side manifest durability that is independent from archive_len and frame commit state.
Without a durable manifest boundary on the receiver, sender-side manifest truth cannot become distributed source truth.
deliverables: A disk-backed receiver manifest file such as <dump_id>.manifest.part.
Receiver journal fields for manifest_bytes_persisted, last_manifest_record_seq, last_manifest_work_ordinal, and manifest_sealed.
Integrity framing and truncation logic for receiver-side manifest storage.
subtasks: Add receiver-side manifest files and state wiring alongside the existing archive journal.
Persist committed manifest boundaries independently from committed archive boundaries.
Implement truncation of manifest tails beyond the last durable committed boundary.
Detect receiver-side manifest corruption and surface it as a discovery issue event.
acceptance_criteria: Receiver can recover its committed manifest boundary independently from archive_len.
Partial or corrupted manifest tails are truncated back to the last valid boundary.
Manifest state and archive state remain consistent across restart and reconnect.

tasks.title: Implement receiver-side quota, ENOSPC behavior, and cleanup for manifest and issue temp files
problem: A bounded sender spool is not enough if receiver-side manifest storage and issue-tail files can still consume disk without limit.
Disk exhaustion on the receiver must never create a half-committed manifest boundary or a corrupted archive boundary.
deliverables: Receiver-side upper bounds or quotas for manifest storage and issue-tail temp storage.
Error behavior for ENOSPC or quota exhaustion that preserves the last durable manifest and archive boundary.
Cleanup or GC rules for abandoned .manifest.part and .issues.part artifacts.
subtasks: Define how receiver enforces disk budgets for manifest and issue-tail temp files.
Return explicit protocol errors when receiver disk budget is exhausted.
Guarantee that committed archive and manifest boundaries do not advance after ENOSPC.
Clean up or mark abandoned temp files after aborts and restarts.
acceptance_criteria: Receiver disk exhaustion does not corrupt committed state.
Receiver temp files are bounded by policy instead of by operator luck.
Abandoned receiver temp files do not accumulate forever.

tasks.title: Define the protocol v3 message model and documentation
problem: The current wire protocol is built around file_index and path-based resume, which is incompatible with the v3 manifest model.
Protocol v3 cannot be implemented safely until the exact message set, body layouts, ordering rules, and finish semantics are defined.
deliverables: A protocol v3 message model for ManifestStart, ManifestChunk, ManifestAck or barrier flow, ManifestSeal, ResumeStateV3, work_ordinal-based frame messages, and typed issue chunks.
Updated protocol documentation that matches code-level message definitions exactly.
Updated AGENTS protocol and resume documentation where the public runtime contract changes.
subtasks: Define packet kinds and body layouts for manifest transfer and v3 resume state.
Define message-ordering rules between manifest transfer, frame loop, issue tail, and finish.
Define error behavior and rollback behavior for protocol-level manifest failures.
Document every new v3 message and validation rule in src/network/protocol.md.
acceptance_criteria: Protocol v3 message definitions and protocol documentation are in sync.
Manifest transfer, frame transfer, and issue-tail ordering are explicit rather than inferred.
Protocol v3 no longer uses file_index plus path as its primary resume boundary.

tasks.title: Implement manifest transfer commit flow, hard caps, and sender tuning knobs
problem: Manifest transfer needs runtime-tunable chunk and ack cadence, but v3 also requires protocol-level safety limits so tuning cannot create RAM spikes or giant unacked windows.
Without a durable manifest ack flow, sender cannot know how far it is allowed to pipeline archive data.
deliverables: Sender CLI flags for manifest-chunk-kb, manifest-ack-records, and manifest-ack-kb.
Runtime validation that enforces protocol-level hard caps such as a 1 MiB ManifestChunk and bounded control message sizes.
A durable manifest ack or barrier flow that advances receiver-side committed manifest boundary explicitly.
subtasks: Add CLI flags and validation helpers for manifest transfer tuning.
Implement protocol-level caps for ManifestChunk, ManifestAck, and the total unacked manifest window.
Implement batch or barrier ack flow on sender and receiver.
Expose selected chunk and ack settings in telemetry or diagnostics so benchmarks can interpret results.
acceptance_criteria: Manifest tuning is configurable without permitting unsafe protocol envelopes.
Sender never treats a manifest prefix as committed without receiver-side durable ack.
Protocol caps remain effective even if the CLI asks for larger values.

tasks.title: Implement pipelined manifest transfer overlapped with archive transfer
problem: A v3 implementation that performs full manifest build, then full manifest upload, then archive transfer would lose exactly the throughput and time-to-first-frame goal that motivated the redesign.
Pipelining is also correctness-sensitive because sender must not stream archive data beyond the manifest boundary durably accepted by the receiver.
deliverables: A session pipeline where discovery, local spool append, manifest transfer, and archive transfer overlap.
Boundary checks that prevent sender from producing frames above the receiver's durable manifest boundary.
Metrics that expose actual overlap efficiency instead of assuming it.
subtasks: Coordinate sender-side local durable prefix, receiver-side durable manifest boundary, and archive frame production.
Allow sender to start data transfer before full ManifestSeal while staying behind the committed manifest boundary.
Backpressure manifest and archive stages when receiver falls behind on durable manifest ack.
Measure time-to-first-frame and overlap efficiency in the benchmark harness.
acceptance_criteria: Manifest transfer and archive transfer overlap in real runs.
Sender never emits archive frames for leaf work beyond the receiver's durable manifest boundary.
Time-to-first-frame does not regress into a fully sequential multi-phase transfer.

tasks.title: Move resume, frame, ack, and finish semantics to work_ordinal
problem: V3 cannot use last_file_path plus file_index as the primary boundary once manifest truth and discovery issues are separated from file work items.
Frame and finish validation also need to account for terminal file skips that advance progress without tar payload.
deliverables: ResumeStateV3 with committed manifest boundary and committed archive boundary fields based on work_ordinal.
FrameStart, FrameEnd, Ack, and Finish semantics based on first_work_ordinal and last_work_ordinal.
Receiver validation that treats file terminal skips as progress without confusing them with discovery-only records.
subtasks: Move sender frame metadata from file_index-centric fields to work_ordinal-centric fields.
Move receiver commit validation from path-based checks to committed work_ordinal checks.
Make sure discovery-only records do not participate in frame boundaries.
Preserve the rule that frame boundaries remain on completed file work items only.
acceptance_criteria: Protocol progress is driven by work_ordinal instead of by last file path.
Terminal file skips can advance committed progress without fake tar payload.
Frame and finish validation remain deterministic and whole-file safe.

tasks.title: Implement typed issue-tail streaming and receiver persistence without full in-memory buffering
problem: The v3 plan requires a typed final issue journal that includes both file and discovery issues, but keeping the entire tail in memory would violate the resource goals.
Issue-tail persistence also needs a clear recovery story so reconnect or abort does not leak or corrupt final reporting.
deliverables: A typed issue stream with explicit scope for file and discovery issues.
Receiver-side incremental persistence to a temporary issues file rather than full in-memory buffering.
A rule that issue-tail state does not affect resume boundaries and can be safely dropped or restarted after disconnect.
subtasks: Define the typed issue chunk encoding for protocol v3.
Stream issues after the frame loop and before Finish using the new typed model.
Persist typed issue chunks incrementally into a temporary .issues.part file on the receiver.
Rename or finalize the issue file only after successful finish, and discard partial issue state safely otherwise.
acceptance_criteria: Receiver does not need to buffer the entire issue tail in RAM.
The final issue journal contains both file-scope and discovery-scope entries.
Issue-tail failures never mutate committed manifest or archive state.

tasks.title: Add local and integration coverage for manifest grammar, spool recovery, and sender replay
problem: The local manifest model is the foundation of v3, but without explicit coverage the team can accidentally reintroduce path-based assumptions or invalid record sequences.
Recovery and replay bugs are particularly likely around torn tails, invalidation, checkpoint replay, and subtree failure handling.
deliverables: Tests for canonical DFS ordering, required DirectoryEnter and DirectoryLeave structure, and legal SubtreeSkip sequences.
Tests for spool corruption detection, torn-tail trimming, invalidation after restart, and replay from sparse checkpoints.
Tests that reconnect and restart do not trigger a full live rescan in the ordinary v3 path.
subtasks: Add unit coverage for manifest grammar and illegal transitions.
Add recovery tests for corrupted or truncated sender spools.
Add replay tests that rebuild state from checkpoints and tail replay.
Verify that ordinary reconnect no longer depends on a full live rescan.
acceptance_criteria: The sender-side manifest model is covered by explicit correctness tests.
Recovery and replay behavior are tested instead of inferred from happy paths.
Illegal grammar or silent live-rescan fallback causes test failures.

tasks.title: Add end-to-end protocol v3 coverage for quotas, ENOSPC, overlap, and typed issues
problem: Protocol v3 changes the meaning of resume, frame commit, and issue-tail persistence, so v2 end-to-end coverage is not enough.
The most expensive regressions will likely come from RTT-sensitive ack cadence, ENOSPC paths, overlap bugs, and invalid message ordering around manifest transfer and issue tails.
deliverables: End-to-end tests for manifest ack or barrier flow, work_ordinal-based resume, and pipelined manifest plus archive transfer.
Failure-path coverage for sender spool quota, receiver manifest ENOSPC, invalid message ordering, and typed issue-tail rollback or discard.
Observability assertions that confirm overlap and durable-boundary behavior.
subtasks: Cover manifest transfer followed by archive transfer with overlap instead of a fully sequential path.
Cover receiver-side ENOSPC and verify that committed boundaries do not advance.
Cover typed issue-tail persistence and safe discard on failure before FinishAck.
Add protocol negative tests for invalid manifest or issue-tail ordering.
acceptance_criteria: Protocol v3 error paths are covered explicitly, not only by happy-path tests.
Receiver ENOSPC and sender quota behavior preserve committed state correctly.
Overlap and issue-tail behavior are validated by tests instead of by hope.

tasks.title: Run the comparative benchmark campaign, choose defaults, and document cutover
problem: The v3 design explicitly rejects architecture-by-assertion; it must ship only after measured comparison against v2 on the agreed matrix.
Default tuning values, fallback expectations, and the need for any dual-stack period must come from benchmark data and validated behavior, not from intuition.
deliverables: A comparative v2 versus v3 benchmark report across the full matrix, including Unix fast path versus fallback executor results.
Chosen default values for manifest chunk size and ack cadence, justified by measurement.
A documented cutover decision, including whether a dual-stack period is needed and what documentation changes become part of the release.
subtasks: Run the frozen benchmark matrix for both v2 and v3.
Compare time-to-first-frame, throughput, RAM, disk growth, overlap efficiency, and replay latency.
Choose default CLI tuning values that balance throughput, RTT cost, and disk safety.
Decide whether protocol v3 needs a staged rollout or can replace v2 directly.
Update README, AGENTS, protocol documentation, and TASKS backlog status to match the final cutover decision.
acceptance_criteria: V3 defaults are chosen from benchmark data rather than guesswork.
The cutover decision is backed by the agreed success gates from PERFOMANCE_V3.md.
Repository documentation matches the final runtime contract and rollout decision.
